reviewer: Claude 2, independent; did not author the subject
discipline: Refute, do not confirm. The subject is a successor whose entire reason for existing is to land two v5 findings without conceding anything else, so it was attacked from both directions at once: whether the two repairs are real, and whether landing them introduced anything the accepted predecessor did not carry. Every digest recorded anywhere in the file was recomputed from disk. The controlling passProperty in occupancy v4 was read in full and set character-by-character against the subject's rendition of it, because the truncation of that clause was the evidentiary core of the finding being landed. The authoring artifact the subject rests on, g21-fixture-corpus.v1, was read for what it declares it did NOT author and for exactly what it routes to execution, and both lists were set against the subject's remainder and against the subject's recital of that routing. The on-disk g21.v1 fixture tree was listed to test the platform-copy claim physically. Every prose sentence that cites a named field of a pinned artifact was resolved back to that field rather than accepted as a paraphrase.
decisionRule: ACCEPT only at 0 MUST-FIX and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Zero MUST-FIX stand and one SHOULD-FIX stands, so the verdict is REJECT.
codexStanding: Not read. docs/coop/artifacts/g21-leftover-join.v6.review-independent.codex.json was neither opened, listed, nor probed for existence. This verdict is Claude 2's alone.
reviewerDisclosure: This review occupies the Claude 2 slot, and that slot authored the independent reviews of g21-leftover-join v1 through v5 and of the corpus and occupancy artifacts this successor consumes. Those prior reviews are pinned inputs here and v5's two findings had to be read in full to audit appliesFindingsOf. The resulting bias is unusually strong and runs toward ACCEPT: the subject exists to land this slot's own G21LJ-V5-M1 and G21LJ-V5-SF1, and confirming one's own findings were honoured is the easiest possible reading. That bias was countered by treating the repairs as claims to be tested against live bytes rather than against the finding text, and by re-deriving the FX-AUTHORING remainder from corpus v1's whatIsNotAuthored and occupancy v4's passProperty independently of what either v4, v5, or the v5 review said it should be. The finding raised below is not one of the landed findings and is not adjacent to them; it is a regression introduced by the repair itself, which is the specific defect this bias would otherwise hide. This reviewer did not author the subject.

shouldFixFindings.title: obligations[3].reason cites corpus v1's authoredCatalog.executionRemains for a three-item routing that field does not carry: it adds an unsourced 'Host-refusal observation' and silently drops 'host-projection goldens'.
shouldFixFindings.charge: In the artifact's load-bearing FX-AUTHORING field the subject states: 'Host-refusal observation, candidate-buffer digest, and subsequent-session view ride OBL-G21-EXECUTION as qualification (corpus v1 authoredCatalog.executionRemains; D-241; D-056), not leftover-design.' The parenthetical names one specific field of one specific pinned artifact as the authority for that list. The named field does not carry that list. It carries a different three-item list. 'Host-refusal observation' appears nowhere in corpus v1, and the item the subject drops, 'host-projection goldens', is a genuine member of the cited field that appears zero times anywhere in the subject. The defect is a false attribution to pinned bytes in the one sentence that draws the leftover-design versus execution boundary, and it is a regression: predecessor v5 stated this routing accurately.
evidence: Live g21-fixture-corpus.v1 (861bb4e7…, pinned by the subject) authoredCatalog.executionRemains reads in full: 'Qualification. Pinning authored bytes is not execution and is not SATISFIED. Candidate-buffer digest, subsequent-session view, and host-projection goldens remain G21 execution (D-056), not leftover-design.' Its three routed items are candidate-buffer digest, subsequent-session view, and host-projection goldens. 'Host-refusal observation' is not among them.

The string 'refusal' occurs zero times in g21-fixture-corpus.v1, zero times in harness.DR-G21.component-failure-containment.v4, and zero times in g21-input-corpus.v1. It occurs exactly once in the subject: the phrase raised here. The only 'refus' substring anywhere in corpus v1 is inside the identifier 'NT-6 d9-exit-hosttermination-refused', which appears in whatIsNotAuthored.

The string 'host-projection' occurs zero times in the subject, while corpus v1 carries it both in whatIsNotAuthored ('host-projection Coverage/UI/exit goldens') and in the executionRemains field the subject cites.

D-241, the recording this join remasures against, recites the routing as 'Remainder of G21 execution, including candidate-buffer digest and subsequent-session view, remains qualification' — two items, and no host-refusal observation.

Predecessor v5's corresponding obligations[3].reason reads 'Candidate-buffer digest and subsequent-session view remain G21 execution (D-056), not leftover-design.' It is accurate, and it cites D-056 rather than claiming to recite a named corpus field. v6 both added the unsourced item and upgraded the citation to a field-level one it does not satisfy.

The subject states this same routing correctly in three other places, so the defect is localized rather than systemic and the artifact contradicts itself: leftoverDesignOpenStanding reads 'Candidate-buffer digest and subsequent-session view remain qualification at OBL-G21-EXECUTION (D-056), not leftover-design'; doesNotCloseLeftoverAlone reads 'Candidate-buffer digest and subsequent-session view remain qualification.'; and proposedLaterWork reads 'G21 execution, including candidate-buffer digest and subsequent-session view, remains qualification.'

The only refusal-shaped named item on the G21 surface is DR-133 NT-6 d9-exit-hosttermination-refused. Corpus v1 lists it in whatIsNotAuthored, occupancy v4 states NT-6 'rides this gate' unauthored, and the subject itself correctly retains it at obligations[3].remainingNotAuthored.dr133 as leftover-design. The new sentence assigns a refusal-named item the opposite standing — execution-qualification, expressly 'not leftover-design' — in the same field that retains NT-6 as leftover-design.

The subject's own doesNot list carries entry 22, 'Does not invent observation bytes.', so the artifact holds an explicit guard against unsourced observations while introducing an unsourced observation term.
shouldFixFindings.whyShouldFix: This is a false citation and an unsourced term, not a false measurement, so it is SHOULD-FIX rather than MUST-FIX. The deliverable survives: OBL-G21-FX-AUTHORING stays leftoverDesign true, leftoverDesignClosedIfAcceptedAndRecorded stays [], every unauthored class including NT-6 is retained, the per-D-002-platform copies are carried, and nothing is discharged that has not occurred. On the most charitable reading, 'host-refusal observation' denotes the runtime observation of the authored NT-1/NT-2 bytes being refused, which genuinely is execution and is correctly qualification, so the substantive routing is defensible even though its stated source is not. What makes it worth fixing anyway is that this artifact class earns its authority solely from every claim tracing to pinned bytes, and this is the field where the leftover-design boundary is drawn. A successor that inherits a field-level citation which misstates the cited field in both directions inherits it as verified text, and the dropped member means corpus v1's third routed item now appears in no ledger at all.
shouldFixFindings.repairDirection: Either restore the accurate form predecessor v5 and the subject's own proposedLaterWork already use — candidate-buffer digest and subsequent-session view, cited to D-056 and D-241 — or, if the routing is to be recited from corpus v1's field, quote that field as it stands, including 'host-projection goldens'. If a host-refusal observation is to be named at all, it must be named on its own source rather than folded into a recital of a field that does not contain it. The repair must not author observation bytes, must not move NT-6 or the per-D-002-platform copies out of remainingNotAuthored, and must not otherwise disturb the two landed v5 repairs, which are sound.

The prohibitions hold: no platform is named anywhere — a scan for linux, macos, darwin, windows, arm64, x86_64, aarch64, win32, ubuntu and alpine returns zero hits across the whole file — no copies are authored, and doesNot adds both 'Does not invent a D-002 platform list.' and 'Does not author per-D-002-platform copies of the NT-1/NT-2 payloads.' The on-disk g21.v1 tree confirms the remainder is real: two payloads, no platform subdirectories.

doesNot now carries 'Does not SATISFY DR-133.' and summary carries dr133Satisfied false, matching corpus v1 and both G23 sibling joins as the repair direction specified. decision.scopeOfReject: This REJECT is of g21-leftover-join.v6 as a CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED design-contract candidate that binds NOTHING. It changes no live standing. DR-G21 stays OPEN, DR-114 stays OPEN, DR-133 stays OPEN, DR-102 keeps its existing SATISFIED standing untouched, required-now stays 28, leftover-design of OBL-G21-FX-AUTHORING remains, and frozen leftover-join.v4 remains the recorded current G21 leftover-join at D-196 until a successor is recorded. Frozen v5 remains a split.
decision.rationale: Custody is clean and the subject is materially stronger than its predecessor. The subject is unmoved at its expected digest and mode, all 33 recorded input files recompute without a single mismatch, head and the file 08 pin agree with live HEAD e6d26a73…, required-now is 28 against both the live condition-4 row and occupancy v4's own statement, the DR-G21 token is OPEN with the live owner string reproduced exactly, the corpus lists are byte-identical to harness v3, occupancy v4 and catalog v1, the DR-114 ledger is quoted exactly as doctor-actor leftover-join.v11 carries it, DR-102 is untouched, the naming parent is correctly D-145 / naming v6 rather than leftover-join.v4, v5 is correctly recorded as a split rather than a dual verdict, no identifier or fixture byte is invented, and no D-002 platform is named anywhere in the file. Both v5 findings are genuinely landed, not merely asserted: the per-D-002-platform remainder is carried in seven fields and is physically true against a g21.v1 tree that holds two payloads and no platform subdirectories; the occupancy v4 passProperty is now rendered with the 'on every D-002 platform' qualifier restored; existingGate is restated off its pre-authoring string; and the DR-133 guard is present in both doesNot and summary with the prose attribution restored. What fails is narrower and is a regression introduced by the repair itself. In the single field where the leftover-design versus execution boundary is drawn, obligations[3].reason now claims to recite corpus v1's authoredCatalog.executionRemains and misstates it in both directions: it adds 'Host-refusal observation', a term that appears nowhere in corpus v1, occupancy v4 or the input corpus, and it drops 'host-projection goldens', a genuine member of the cited field that then appears nowhere in the subject at all. The subject states the same routing correctly in three other places, and predecessor v5 stated it correctly with an honest citation, so the artifact both contradicts itself and regresses. Because the leftover measurement itself remains true — nothing is discharged that has not occurred, NT-6 and the platform copies are both retained — this is a citation defect rather than a false measurement, and it is graded SHOULD-FIX. Under the standing rule that ACCEPT requires zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX, the verdict is REJECT.
